Divine Vengeance often gets misused for its spectacle - its 10-round duration demands tactical foresight.

GMs: Before casting Divine Vengeance, make them state their tactical plan to exploit its 10-round duration effectively.

Ran it differently at your table? Drop it in the comments. @bizzalgames70

Mimic's Adhesive trait surprises players who touch it - they become Grappled.

DMs: Remind players that a Mimic's Adhesive trait grapples on contact; use ranged attacks to exploit its 12 AC and 20-foot speed.

Send this to the rules-lawyer in your group. @bizzalgames70

Potion of Giant Strength's drawback surprises many - 1d3 Strength drained after the effect ends.

Judges: Hand this out when a player needs that +4 Strength boost to turn the tide, but remind them of the 1d3 Strength drain.

Send this to the rules-lawyer in your group. @bizzalgames70

Advantage and Disadvantage can simplify decision-making - they do not stack, ever.

GMs: Enforce the rule - advantage and disadvantage never stack; they cancel each other out, leaving just one roll.

Daily tabletop RPG rulings. Follow @bizzalgames70 for one a day.

Spell Check results surprise many - under 12 usually fails, but you keep the spell unless you roll a natural.

Judges: Remind them that a Spell Check under 12 usually fails, but they can keep trying unless they roll a natural 1.

Send this to the rules-lawyer in your group. @bizzalgames70

Basilisk earns its stakes fast.

GMs: Remind them that a DC 15 CON save means petrification isn't just a possibility - it's a probability.

One ruling a day, no fluff. Follow @bizzalgames70.

Ability Scores often mislead players into thinking higher is always better - the modifier.

DMs: Remind players that a +3 modifier from a 16 Dexterity is more impactful than the score itself.

One ruling a day, no fluff. Follow @bizzalgames70.

Monster Summoning surprises with its risk of turning foes - a botched control roll can make the summoned.

Judges: Use Monster Summoning's 20-foot range to shift the encounter's balance, but remember a failed control roll invites chaos.

Hourglass Of The Black Sands extends spell duration unpredictably - 1d4 rounds longer once per day.

GMs: Use the Hourglass Of The Black Sands to extend a critical spell by 1d4 rounds when it matters most.

Save this for your next session. Daily rulings: @bizzalgames70

Frame a Sphinx of Valor encounter with a timer so the party must trade certainty for speed.

DMs: Set a visible 10-round countdown timer to highlight the Sphinx of Valor's Arcane Prowl and force decisive player actions.

Tendrilagon's camouflage is more effective than players expect - +10 to hide checks in hay.

Judges: Remind them the Tendrilagon takes double damage from fire - if they can't remember that, they deserve to be swallowed whole.

Random Encounters catch parties off guard - they occur every 10 minutes on a d6 roll of 1.

GMs: Roll a d6 every 10 minutes; a 1 means a random encounter - keep your players' torches burning and ready.
